name: Ring-billed Gull
rangeDescription: North america; winters to southern mexico, bahamas, and greater antilles
description: Fairly small gull, common and widespread throughout most of North America. Breeding adults are white-headed with a bold black ring around the bill; nonbreeding adults have smudgy brown markings on the head.

name: Creamy-bellied Gnatcatcher
rangeDescription: Lowlands of southeastern brazil to eastern paraguay and northeastern argentina
description: Distinctive gnatcatcher. Males have a glossy black cap and are gray above with a white face and yellow-washed underparts.

name: Madagascar Buzzard
rangeDescription: Woodland and savanna of madagascar
description: Typical brown buzzard that is endemic to Madagascar. Found throughout the island in many different habitats, though absent from pure grassland.

name: Cabanis's Wren
rangeDescription: Southern mexico (oaxaca) southward on the pacific slope to northwestern costa rica; locally on the caribbean slope from southern mexico (chiapas) to honduras
description: Small, skulking wren of foothills and lowlands in southern Mexico and Central America. Found in forest edges, second-growth thickets, and brushy fields with cane grass.

name: Cebu Boobook
rangeDescription: Philippines (cebu)
description: A medium-sized owl of wooded areas on the island of Cebu. Head and upperparts dark brown and indistinctly barred.

name: Mindoro Hornbill
rangeDescription: Mindoro (central philippines)
description: A fairly large bird of lowland and foothill forest on Mindoro. Small for a hornbill.

name: Olive-spotted Hummingbird
rangeDescription: Far southeastern colombia to eastern ecuador, northeastern peru, and northwestern brazil
description: Medium-sized, drab-greenish hummingbird. Dull green above, with diffuse olive spotting underneath, and a white belly.

name: Tawny Lark
rangeDescription: Semiarid central plateau of india
description: A pale yellowish-brown lark with a long, spiky crest and a thick, short bill. The heavy streaking on the upperparts contrasts strongly with the rest of the plumage.

name: Chestnut-and-black Weaver
rangeDescription: Varied wooded habitats from guinea to eastern nigeria
description: Males have an unusual and distinctive coloration: mostly black, with a chestnut back and belly. Females are brownish-olive, with paler underparts, and a rufous tinge to the rump.

name: Rufous-tailed Flycatcher
rangeDescription: Wooded hills and mountains of jamaica
description: A medium-sized woodland species that prefers moist forests where it typically “flycatches” from perches in thick foliage beneath the canopy. Note its bright rusty tail and the extensive rust on its wings.

name: Scintillant Hummingbird
rangeDescription: Humid montane forest of costa rica and western panama
description: Small hummingbird, unique orange throat distinguishes male from all other hummingbirds in limited range. Female less obvious; she has speckled throat, orangey flanks, and all-rufous tail with black band and buffy tips.

name: St. Vincent Wren
rangeDescription: St. vincent (lesser antilles)
description: Small brownish wren found only on St. Vincent.

name: Least Pygmy-Owl
rangeDescription: Eastern paraguay to southeastern brazil and northeastern argentina (misiones)
description: Very small rufous owl with white spots flecked on rich brown head, a white belly streaked with rufous and white spots on the back. Similar to Ferruginous Pygmy-Owl, which has a streaked rather than spotted head and a longer tail.

name: Taiwan Bamboo-Partridge
rangeDescription: Taiwan
description: Medium-sized, mostly brownish terrestrial bird with a slate-gray head and neck, dark orange throat, and rusty spots on sides and wings. Endemic to Taiwan., where it inhabits lowland and foothill forests with undergrowth and densely vegetated edges, where difficult to see.

name: Chestnut-sided Warbler
rangeDescription: Eastern north america; winters guatemala to panama (casual northern south america)
description: Breeding birds show yellow cap, black triangle under eye, streaked back and reddish-brown sides. Looks remarkably different in fall with distinctive lime green above and gray below with bold white eyering.

name: Seychelles Swiftlet
rangeDescription: Seychelles (mahé, praslin, and la digue)
description: Small gray swift with a slightly paler rump and belly. Flight is fast but erratic, with the wings pushed forward.

name: Great Spotted Cuckoo
rangeDescription: Southwestern palearctic and sub-saharan africa
description: Distinctive, boldly patterned cuckoo with a spiffy crest and white-spotted wings. Adult has a gray crest and gray-brown back.

name: South Island Saddleback
rangeDescription: Formerly widespread on south island (new zealand); by 1950s confined to south cape islands, now introduced to additional outlying islands
description: A medium-sized songbird endemic to New Zealand, confined to predator-free offshore islands and South Island mainland sanctuaries. Glossy black plumage with distinct chestnut saddle across the back, which gives the bird its name.

name: Tawny-backed Fantail
rangeDescription: Montane forest of buru (southern moluccas)
description: A small brown songbird with a long tail that is often cocked and regularly fanned. Rich rufous on the back and rump, with a contrastingly darker pale-tipped tail.

name: Eastern Bearded-Greenbul
rangeDescription: Cameroon to eastern democratic republic of the congo, northern angola, and far western uganda
description: A large greenbul often found in family groups or flocks in forest and forest edge with other bearded-greenbuls. Like all bearded-greenbuls, will sometimes puff out throat feathers.
